# skycloak_cluster_public_access (Resource)

Manages whether a cluster's public hostname is served. Only one resource should manage a cluster's public access. Turning public access off needs an Enterprise plan with private networking, and the API refuses it unless Azure private link is enabled and ready, because the private hostname is then the only way in. Order this resource after `skycloak_cluster_private_link`. Destroy turns public access back on, which lets the private link be disabled afterwards. The API key needs the `clusters:read` and `clusters:write` scopes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Requires an Enterprise plan. Turning public access off is refused unless
# Azure private link is enabled and ready, so depend on the private link.
resource "skycloak_cluster_public_access" "example" {
  cluster_id    = skycloak_cluster.example.id
  public_access = false

  depends_on = [skycloak_cluster_private_link.example]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster ID. Immutable.
- `public_access` (Boolean) Whether the cluster's public hostname is served. When `false` the cluster is reachable only through its private link hostname.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite ID `cluster_id/public-access`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import skycloak_cluster_public_access.example 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
```
